Topic: Mastering the Cross Product: From 2D Geometry to 3D Space

Target audience: University students (Engineering/Physics/Computer Science)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Warm-up: Orientation and Determinants

Lecture lines:
Cross product calculates area spanned by two vectors.
The determinant finds this area as signed quantity.
Positive area means counter-clockwise rotation, negative is clockwise.

Planned animations:
Create a 2D grid in #FFFFFF color as the base.
Flash the 2D grid to highlight the initial orientation.
Calculate the determinant and show it as a scalar #FF0000.

Section: section_2 — The 3D Cross Product: Definition and Right-Hand Rule

Lecture lines:
In 3D, cross product produces a normal vector.
Use the Right-Hand Rule to find its direction.
Curl your fingers from vector A to vector B.

Planned animations:
Draw two vectors v and w in #00FF00 and #0000FF.
Render the resulting cross product vector as #FFFF00.
Rotate the vectors to demonstrate the Right-Hand Rule clearly.

Section: section_3 — The Determinant Formula for 3D

Lecture lines:
We represent this operation using a 3x3 matrix.
Place basis vectors i, j, k at the top.
Determinant expansion computes the resulting vector components.
Remember the anti-commutative property: A x B = -B x A.
Example: i x j gives the unit vector k.

Planned animations:
Display the matrix components in #FFFFFF.
Highlight sub-determinants using #FF00FF boxes for calculation.
Finalize the formula by connecting terms with #FFFFFF lines.

Section: section_4 — Geometric Meaning and Physical Applications

Lecture lines:
Magnitude of cross product equals |A||B|sin(theta).
Torque is the physical application of this concept.
Torque equals the radius vector times force vector.

Planned animations:
Represent a parallelepiped with #FF8000 edges.
Highlight the volume using a semi-transparent #808080 fill.
Apply a transformation pulse to signify volume change.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Quick Check

Lecture lines:
Cross product result is always a vector.
Dot product result is always a scalar value.
Changing vector order reverses the resulting vector direction.

Planned animations:
Display summary points in #FFFFFF.
Flash each point as it appears for recap.
Show a checkmark animation in #00FF00 for completion.

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
